title: Platform Uptime + FinOps Roadmap Huddle
summary: Quarterly check-in focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents over the last quarter, and a proposed runway + pilot acceleration plan. Agreed to run a targeted throughput benchmark, share detailed cost model, and align on security docs (SOC2 scope questions).
action_items: Maya Chen: Share detailed cost model spreadsheet and per-route token breakdown by 2026-03-30
Liam O'Connor: Schedule and run 48-hour throughput benchmark on customer dev cluster (dedicated pool config) w/ prefix caching enabled - target by 2026-04-08
Nadia Patel: Provide recent oncall postmortem and example traces for two latency spikes by 2026-03-28
next_steps: Redwood to send cost model + quantization suggestions
Setup bench run and invite AeroFin infra team
Customer to confirm decision criteria for Dedicated commit vs burst capacity
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC · 54 mins / Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Anand (Redwood) — Carlos Rios, Nadia Patel, Owen Park (AeroFin Labs)

Summary (auto): QBR-style health check: usage up 2.3x year-over-quarter, cost spike on week of Feb 8th due to unbatched short-run reranks; two incidents of 500ms+ P95 in EU region. Discussed dedicated capacity vs optimized hosted routing, and next steps for a short benchmark.

00:00 - Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. I know we have a packed agenda — run through last quarter, then we'll jump into the cost model and a proposed pilot acceleration.
00:18 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): Yeah, thanks Maya. Quick note, we had a fairly busy week in Feb where our internal dashboards spiked, we saw a couple of 503s and some elevated latencies. I want to understand root cause and what the recommended levers are.
00:37 - Speaker 1 (Maya): Totally. Liam from our SE team will walk through what we saw on the infra side and some configuration knobs — batching, prefix cache and autoscale.
00:50 - Speaker 3 (Liam): Hola. So the short summary: your traffic pattern has lots of short prompt reranks interleaved with long streaming chat. That mix is what causes the inefficiency — continuous small requests prevent high batching. Where we saw the Feb spike, KV cache miss rate was higher because the prompt shaping changed, and the hosted pool hit throttling around 10am UTC on Feb 9. It manifested as higher P95.
01:15 - Speaker 4 (Nadia): Quick Q — when you say throttling, is that our account hitting concurrency limit or is that internal to the serving runtime?
01:24 - Speaker 3 (Liam): A bit of both. The routing policy had us on a medium-cost pool with lower burst headroom; plus the request pattern didn't utilize prefix/KV caching as much. So auto-batching wasn't able to reach target batch sizes.
01:40 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): Okay that makes sense. From Ops perspective, we prefer predictable latency even if cost is a bit higher; we wanted to hear the tradeoffs.
01:50 - Speaker 1 (Maya): Right — so the three levers we usually propose: 1) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) for core endpoints, 2) routing policies to route latency-sensitive routes to the low-latency tier and non-critical to cost-optimized tier, and 3) model-level optimizations — quantization or lower sequence length configs for rerankers.
02:10 - Speaker 5 (Owen): On the finance side, our CFO will want a clear delta on cost if we move to Dedicated — can you provide an example commit tier and what the per-token model looks like?
02:22 - Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we'll send a cost model. We'll include a delta for reserved 3x throughput commit vs hosted pay-as-you-go, with sensitivity to effective batching rate.
02:34 - Speaker 3 (Liam): Also recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for the rerank route — we've seen 30-45% token cost reductions for workloads with stable prefixes. Caveat: effectiveness drops if the input prompts are highly dynamic.
02:55 - Speaker 4 (Nadia): We need to vet the security side — what about KMS integration and audit logs for Dedicated? We have strict PCI-ish handling for some data slices.
03:06 - Speaker 1 (Maya): For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and full audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 scope and a snippet of the audit log retention policy.
03:18 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): Perfect. Also curious about SSO and RBAC — our engineering org needs per-team keys and scoped routes.
03:27 - Speaker 6 (Priya): We can set up RBAC via our Console — create per-route tokens and team-level roles, and integrate with SAML SSO; we'll share a short how-to doc.
03:40 - Speaker 3 (Liam): On the reliability front, quick thought: if you go dedicated, you can pin model versions which helps avoid surprising rollouts that change latency. Also plan canary rollouts with auto-fallback to a smaller model if latencies exceed SLO.
03:59 - Speaker 4 (Nadia): Can you give an example SLO you typically see for a dedicated pool? Like P95 < 250ms for short requests?
04:06 - Speaker 3 (Liam): We typically guarantee P95 targets as part of Dedicated SLAs; realistic numbers depend on model size and sequence length. For a mid-size reranker quantized profile we often hit P95 ~120-180ms at steady state. We'll include benchmark numbers.
04:26 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): Great — I want to loop in our infra folks for the benchmark. Owen will coordinate.
04:33 - Speaker 5 (Owen): Yep. For the benchmark, we need to reproduce peak mix — short rerank bursts with occasional streaming. Can Redwood capture that in a bench script?
04:41 - Speaker 3 (Liam): Absolutely, we'll provide a bench harness with replay and options for KV cache stubbing. We suggest a 48-hour run to capture autoscale behavior.
04:53 - Speaker 1 (Maya): On the cost side, we noticed a pattern: a small set of routes account for 78% of tokens but only 32% of revenue — that signals opportunity to right-size batching and TTL on caches. We'll show route-level token burn in the cost model.
05:12 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): Hmm, that mirrors our internal numbers. Any quick wins we can do without changing infra?
05:20 - Speaker 3 (Liam): Prompt engineering and consolidating short requests into batched calls. Also consider increasing TTL for cache items where semantics permit.
05:29 - Speaker 4 (Nadia): About telemetry — can we get per-token latency breakdown in Console? We need trace IDs to jump from app spans to Redwood traces.
05:39 - Speaker 6 (Priya): Yes, we support tracing hooks; we'll share an example of linking a request-id header to Console traces and show a sample dashboard.
05:51 - Speaker 5 (Owen): On procurement — if we go dedicated, what's the contract length and penalties? Also, can we do a short pilot without a long-term commit?
06:01 - Speaker 1 (Maya): We offer 30-day pilots on Dedicated as an evaluation (metered) and then commit options for 6/12/24 months with tiered discounts. We'll include contract term examples in the follow-up.
06:15 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): Security detail — you mentioned SOC2. Are there any gaps in attestation for our auditors we should know about?
06:23 - Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll pull the SOC2 summary. For PCI-ish controls you'll want to review the encryption key lifecycle and data residency notes; we'll flag any special handling.
06:35 - Speaker 3 (Liam): One other technical note: quantized model variants can reduce GPU memory and cost but may introduce subtle quality diffs. We recommend running quality evals on your golden prompts before switching. Redwood Optimize can run evaluation harnesses and surface regressions.
06:55 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): Can you run a quick eval with our rerank test set as part of the benchmark?
07:03 - Speaker 3 (Liam): Yes, include your eval suite when we schedule the bench run. We'll produce both perf and quality matrices.
07:12 - Speaker 6 (Priya): Ok, let's recap. Action items: Maya to send cost workbook; Liam to spin bench and invite Nadia/Owen; Nadia to share traces/postmortem; Priya to share RBAC/SSO how-to; customer to confirm which endpoints they want in scope for Dedicated pilot.
07:34 - Speaker 4 (Nadia): One small ask — can we get a targeted architecture diagram showing where KMS sits and how logs flow? That helps our auditors.
07:42 - Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll attach a diagram in the email.
07:46 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): Timeline note — we want decision-ready materials by April 12 to brief finance. Is that feasible?
07:53 - Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, that's reasonable. We'll aim to have cost model and bench results draft by April 8, final by April 12.
08:02 - Speaker 5 (Owen): Sounds good. Anything else on roadmap?
08:07 - Speaker 1 (Maya): We briefly touched on model rollouts and guardrails — we'll include recommended rollout plan and rollback windows.
08:14 - Speaker 3 (Liam): Also note, if you move some non-critical workloads to a cost-optimized model tier, you can free capacity in Dedicated for low-latency traffic — it's a routing policy thing more than hardware.
08:31 - Speaker 2 (Carlos): That seems like a good middle ground.
08:35 - Speaker 6 (Priya): Final: we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the bench and include the docs pack.
08:42 - Speaker 1 (Maya): Thank you all. We'll email the next steps and owners. Appreciate the time.

End notes: transcript contains occasional mislabels; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KV cache sometimes appears as "K-V cash"), and product names abbreviated. Shared artifacts referenced: cost-model.xlsx (link to be sent), bench-harness.zip (link), SOC2-summary.pdf (link).
